topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture objectives and outline the framework of cancer hallmarks across tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades enable cancer cells to achieve growth signal independence.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial malignancies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic alterations prevent cells from exiting the cell cycle and executing terminal differentiation in blood and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through genetic disruptions of the apoptotic machinery.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor cells circumvent normal division limits and senescence through telomere maintenance and stress response evasion.

topics.label: Complex hallmarks and cancer metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex tissue-level hallmarks and examine the mechanisms and drivers of altered tumor metabolism.

topics.label: Angiogenesis induction in tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how developing tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to sustain oxygen and nutrient supply.

topics.label: Mechanisms, tracking, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the multi-step metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cell monitoring, and the genomic features of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarize the collective role of cancer hallmarks and conclude the lecture.
